items.a_statement: IIT predicts that loss and recovery of consciousness is associated with breakdown and recovery of information integration capacity, measurable via the perturbational complexity index (PCI) derived from TMS-EEG responses.

The PSC operates at a definite spatio-temporal grain (local cortical neuron groups over ~100 ms intervals); perturbations at the appropriate grain change experience, fixing the mechanism scale of consciousness.

The global neuronal workspace is anatomically constituted by long-distance cortico-cortical connections arising from pyramidal neurons in layers II-III, densely distributed in prefrontal and parietal cortices.
Only mechanisms that specify integrated information—information generated by the whole above and beyond its parts, making it irreducible—can contribute to consciousness.
The physical substrate of consciousness has a definite spatial grain, timescale, and state-space determined by maxima of cause–effect power, identifiable empirically via perturbation and observation.

The PSC is a bounded complex of elements with maximal integrated information; elements outside this boundary (e.g., cerebellar neurons, peripheral sensory/motor pathways, basal ganglia loops) do not directly contribute to consciousness despite influencing cortical activity.
Conscious access is marked by a threshold-dependent nonlinear ignition event (~300 ms) in which activity either self-amplifies to ignite the entire workspace network or decays subliminally.
Two distinct consciousness computations are posited: C1 (global availability/reportability) and C2 (self-monitoring/metacognition), which can dissociate empirically.
The richness and level of consciousness increase with the diversity and specialization of causal connections; homogeneous connectivity reduces consciousness.
Existence and consciousness must be evaluated from the intrinsic perspective of the entity itself, not from the perspective of an external observer.
Conscious access is distinct from selective attention; selection and global broadcast availability are separable processes.
The global workspace is a substrate-independent computational architecture: machines with the right functional organization could instantiate conscious computation.
Experience is unified and irreducible to non-interdependent components; integration is an axiomatic property of every experience.
The locus of conscious processing is a large-scale prefrontal-parietal (and cingulate/temporal) cortical network, not posterior sensory cortices alone.
The GNW is substrate-dependent in that it is grounded in specific neuroanatomical recurrent connectivity in the human brain, not any substrate.
The maximally irreducible conceptual structure (MICS) generated by a complex is identical to its experience; its quantity is specified by Φ-max (integrated information).

High Φmax (and thus consciousness) requires convergent-divergent integration; feedforward, modular architectures like the cerebellum cannot form a large complex and are excluded from the conscious substrate.
Conscious information is not transmitted or broadcast from one brain region to another; the locus of consciousness is intrinsic to the PSC, not a relay or global broadcast.

The quality of experience corresponds to the Φ-structure (cause–effect structure of distinctions and relations), and the quantity of experience corresponds to Φ, the sum of integrated information of distinctions and relations.

Every property of an experience is identical to a property of the cause–effect structure specified by a substrate satisfying IIT's postulates; the identity is between intrinsic (subjective) and extrinsic (objective) existence, not between two substances.
C1 (global availability) and C2 (self-monitoring/meta-cognition) are orthogonal, independently variable dimensions of conscious computation.
Without a functional global neuronal workspace, cortical representations cannot be broadcast and are not experienced; functional connectivity of GNW is a necessary condition for consciousness.
Mechanisms that do not generate integrated information do not exist from the intrinsic perspective of a system; integrated information is the threshold condition for causal/experiential existence.
Digital computers running von Neumann architectures are not conscious even if they simulate cognition; the architecture of the substrate determines consciousness.
An experience is identical to the cause–effect structure (Φ-structure) unfolded from a maximal substrate; quality and quantity of experience are completely specified by the MICS and Φ value.
A feed-forward system functionally equivalent to a conscious complex is not conscious, because functional equivalence without intrinsic integrated information is insufficient for experience.
The exclusion postulate restricts the locus of consciousness to a single maximally irreducible system (complex), not any subset or superset.

IIT predicts that the duration of a conscious instant is definite and sustained over tens to hundreds of milliseconds, not transient or phasic, as required by the exclusion postulate governing the cause–effect structure of the PSC.
Consciousness requires intrinsic, integrated, irreducible cause–effect power within the substrate itself, independent of any external observer.

Conscious access has a late temporal signature (>300 ms), with massive amplification of gamma-band power, long-distance phase synchrony, and causal propagation; early responses do not constitute conscious access.

note: A∈{IIT,GNWT} drawn seeded from 43 claims (target 30; corpus supports ≤43). candidates = 5 distractors + 1 reference-match (or 6 distractors when A has no cross-theory partner → answer=none).
